questions.question: Your cell phone rings while you are driving and you do not have a hands-free device. What should you do?

options.text: Answer the call because it might be an emergency.
Let it go to voicemail.
Check the number before answering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go to voicemail.
questions.explanation: Do not use a cell phone while driving without a hands-free device. It is illegal for young drivers to use any cell phone while driving, except in emergencies. Even with a hands-free device, it is better to let calls go to voicemail to avoid distractions.

questions.question: You see a vehicle stopped on the right shoulder with its hazard lights on. What should you do?

options.text: Change to the left lane and speed up.
Slow down and pass carefully.
Stop until you see what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see hazard lights. There may be a crash or emergency ahead. Stop to help if someone asks, or pass very carefully.

questions.question: When must drivers wear a seat belt?

options.text: Not if the vehicle was made before 1978.
Not if driving a limousine.
Always. Not wearing one can result in a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always. Not wearing one can result in a ticket.
questions.explanation: All drivers must wear seat belts. You can receive a ticket for not wearing one.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone.
For picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping allowed.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Dangerous only in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Use extra care when backing up.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: When all vehicles travel at the same speed.
When one lane travels faster than other lanes.
When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one vehicle travels faster or slower than other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when drivers do not match the speed of other traffic. Driving faster or slower than surrounding vehicles increases crash risk. Slow driving can cause rear-end crashes or force others to swerve.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they left the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they left the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibration to warn tired or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It frustrates drivers behind you, who may make risky moves to pass. Drive with traffic flow and follow the speed limit.

questions.question: Reaction time slows after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, and makes you less alert. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and the movement of other vehicles.

questions.question: Speeding too much:

options.text: Saves time so you arrive faster.
Helps you avoid obstacles.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to bad decisions.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your:

options.text: Fog lights only.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Wait for fog to clear before driving if possible. If you must drive in fog, go slowly and use your windshield wipers and low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does a blue painted curb mean?

options.text: Parking allowed for no more than 15 minutes.
Parking only when picking up or dropping off passengers.
Parking for people with disabilities who have a special placard or plate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking for people with disabilities who have a special placard or plate.
questions.explanation: A blue curb is for people with disabilities or drivers of disabled people who have a disabled person placard or special license plate.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and focus.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert and careful. Slow down when you see this light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Road curve ahead.
Right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns drivers that another road crosses the highway.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if pedestrians wave to the driver.
Only if pedestrians are not using their phones.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at a crosswalk to yield to any pedestrians or vehicles in the intersection. You can proceed carefully only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow signal at an intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed but watch for other vehicles.
Stop before you cross.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down and stay alert before entering the intersection. Yield to any pedestrians, bicyclists, or vehicles. You do not need to stop for a flashing yellow light.

questions.question: You must tell the DMV within five days if you:

options.text: Get a traffic ticket.
Sell or give your vehicle to someone else.
Paint your vehicle a different color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sell or give your vehicle to someone else.
questions.explanation: By law, you must contact the DMV within five days after you sell or transfer your vehicle to someone else.

questions.question: Which of these is against the law?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass when you cannot see far ahead to pass safely. You cannot pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, where signs say no passing, where there is a solid yellow line on your side, or when the car ahead stopped for a pedestrian.

questions.question: Before you change lanes or pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Signal before you change lanes.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Always signal to tell other drivers what you plan to do. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move your vehicle left or right.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Annoy drivers with slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests as you approach a work zone.

questions.question: If you have an emergency and must stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the next car.
Pull to the side, turn on emergency lights, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side, turn on emergency lights, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder of an interstate, turn on your emergency lights and stay inside your vehicle if you can. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because cars travel so fast.

questions.question: What usually causes a wheel to lock up and skid?

options.text: Braking hard when driving slowly.
Braking lightly when driving slowly.
Braking hard when driving fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking hard when driving fast.
questions.explanation: A locked wheel skid usually happens when you brake too hard while driving fast. Use your brakes gently and gradually.

questions.question: After you sell your vehicle, you must tell the DMV within ____ days.

options.text: Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Five
questions.explanation: When you sell or transfer a vehicle, you must tell the DMV within five days.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines are between lanes of traffic, what does this mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines between lanes mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Why should you look carefully for motorcycles before changing lanes?

options.text: They are small and hard to see.
They have the right-of-way at all intersections.
It is illegal for motorcycles to share lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are small and hard to see.
questions.explanation: Check carefully for motorcycles when changing lanes because they are small and can easily hide in your blind spots.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic flow?

options.text: Slowing down to look at an accident.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at an accident.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at accidents or other unusual things causes traffic jams and should be avoided.

questions.question: If you have a green light but cars block the intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Wait outside the intersection until it clears.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
Move to another lane and go around the traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until it clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection if you cannot get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.
